task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 17, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper explainer answering why a furniture maker's freight surcharge rose while nearby pump prices were falling.

facts.text: Willow Splice Furniture's August 2026 shipping invoice from Dovetail Freight carries an 8% fuel surcharge, compared with 5% in July.
The underlying freight charge for the compared shipment is unchanged at $1,200.
The surcharge is therefore $96 in August and $60 in July, making freight plus surcharge $1,296 and $1,260.
The difference is $36; the change from 5% to 8% is three percentage points applied to base freight, not an 8% rise in the entire previous bill.
The contract sets each month's surcharge from the previous month's average reading of the fictional North Fen Diesel Index.
The August surcharge reflects July's index, while the lower pump prices observed by the furniture maker were from August.
The monthly index covers a defined regional group of diesel outlets rather than the single filling station nearest the factory.
The index can move differently from an individual carrier's fuel purchases or a particular truck's consumption.
The surcharge formula does not separately match a fuel receipt to each customer's shipment.
The base freight rate is reviewed quarterly under a separate part of the contract.
The compared figures exclude separately agreed unloading or storage services, none of which is priced in the supplied example.
Furniture maker Teri Quell says she must quote delivery costs to customers before the final monthly surcharge is known.
Quell said, "My customer wants one delivery price. My carrier's bill arrives with a moving part."
Carrier manager Oren Brill says the lag gives customers one published surcharge for a whole month rather than changing it with each fill-up.
Brill said, "A monthly rule is easier to quote, but it will not always look like today's pump sign."
The next surcharge has not been announced, so the observed August pump decline does not establish its exact level.
Other customers may have fixed-price or differently indexed freight contracts; this formula is not universal.
The carrier has not supplied a complete margin analysis showing whether the surcharge exactly offsets its changing fuel costs.
Willow Splice ships assembled furniture on reusable racks and schedules most deliveries in weekly groups.
The report supplies no evidence of coordinated freight pricing or a change in the delivered furniture's quality.

forbidden_additions: An 8% increase in the whole old bill or a surcharge calculated from that day's local pump price
A known next-month surcharge or audited exact cost recovery
